To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a substantial increase in space can be achieved by reducing to a single level a non-homogeneous store composed of a fast (core) memory and a slow (disk) memory.

(1) the reduction to one-level store of a fast and slow memory system is possible; (2) the space available in slow storage may be increased substantially by the use of this technique; and (3) the price paid for the increased space is a slow down of the computer, which varies from a few percent to a factor of ten depending on the number and size of pages available in fast memory and on the nature of the application programs.

(a) the scheme permits an increase in the memory space available to a list-structured language; (b) the space is obtained by reducing a nonhomogeneous to a one-level store, the reduction is performed by a page replacement program; (c) the price of the extra space is an increase in the execution time; and (d) the increase is not excessive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of increasing the amount of information which can be processed by a given computer, by using an appropriate organization of its memory.
the problem of increasing the memory space available for list-structured data, without increasing the cost of a computer system.
an efficient use of a nonhomogeneous memory composed of fast and slow stores.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scheme described is a practical and efficient method for increasing the memory space available to a list-structured data processing language.
this technique is a good one for a computer with a small fast memory.
the scheme is practical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the price of the increase in memory space was about 1 to 10 in computer time.
a 32K computer with 32 pages in the fast store has the capability of a 32M machine without any increase in the number of instructions or in the number of registers.
a substantial increase in the memory space is possible at a moderate price in computer time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scheme is feasible and that the price of additional space can be reduced to a level compatible with practical use.
the scheme can be implemented without any change in the language.
the reduction of memory space is a very effective means for increasing the efficiency of list-processing languages.
